name: manual_31b333
claim: Mnemonic for the portable-memory security invariant: 'secure persistent memory = persistently secure memory.' Memory that persists across sessions is only as trustworthy as the discipline that keeps it clean on every single write -- not a one-time cleanup. Tracked memory (episodic/semantic JSONL, rendered lessons, working notes) names categories only; exact private/local values live off-repo and are loaded by guards at runtime, never hardcoded even inside the rule that forbids them.

decisions.notes: Closing distillation for the 2026-07-18 PT PR #256/#258/#260 arc, requested verbatim by the user as the session's final wrap-up mnemonic. Cross-references the fuller doctrine already captured in lesson_6c176e735ab4 (self-quoting-paradox fix), lesson_0a498556c5a0 (day-arc v2-readiness synthesis), and Codex's closure work: .agent/memory/semantic/DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md 'Cybersecurity / OpSec / SecOps' section, .agent/memory/working/COORDINATION_CLOSURE_PACKET_2026-07-18.md, and orama-system docs/v2/47-portable-memory-local-topology-invariant.md (commit b6fea437). OpSec = the discipline of not letting your own operational output (memory, logs, board notes, grep results) reveal what you're protecting; SecOps = the tooling/process that enforces and verifies that discipline (repo_hygiene.py, the local-only registry loader, the all-ref blob scanner). Today's whole arc was both at once: agents practicing OpSec while building the SecOps tooling to prove it.
